description: Published architecture of the hand and wrist muscles, used to draw each muscle belly at its measured size. Keys are muscles or per-digit compartments (FDS2 = flexor digitorum superficialis to digit 2; DI1 = first dorsal interosseous; L1 = first lumbrical). Actuators link here through architecture_id in anatomy.json.
choices: Belly length: cadaver muscle length (Lieber 1990/1992, Jacobson 1992, Patil 2021). Fiber and muscle lengths are normalized to sarcomere length 2.2 um.

Volume: in vivo MRI volume (Holzbaur 2007) for forearm muscles; FDS, FDP, and EDC compartments split the whole-muscle MRI volume by Lieber's cadaver mass fractions. Hand muscles use cadaver volumes: Jacobson 1992 (interossei, lumbricals) and Mirakhorlo 2016 for all thenar and hypothenar muscles, which are not directly comparable with MRI values.
conflicts: ECRL belly length: 9.4 cm in cadavers (Lieber 1990) versus 22.2 cm on MRI (Holzbaur 2007). The cadaver value is used.
MRI volumes are about 1.5-3x cadaver mass / 1.056 g/cm3 (FDS: 74 versus about 38 cm3).
Hand volumes: Kerkhof 2018 is 2-3x Mirakhorlo 2016 (AdP 17.0 versus about 6.2 cm3); each is a single cadaver.
Max force: Saul 2015 re-derived forces from MRI volume at 50.8 N/cm2, 2-5x Holzbaur 2005. MyoHand lumbrical forces (48-98 N) far exceed Jacobson PCSA x specific tension (3-6 N).

MUSIC's maximum forces for its five added muscles cite Holzbaur 2005 and Del Santo 2007, neither of which contains these muscles, so they are untraced. The values are not reproduced here because MUSIC has no license.

Several tendon slack lengths changed from Holzbaur 2005. Values cross-checked against MOBL_ARMS_41.osim (third-party GitHub copy, ENGNajafpourBio/Parkinson-Tremor-Simulation-OpenSim) — they match Table 3.
